title: DNA links between the Volga-Ural region and the conquerors
fact_summary: A 2022 study of 6th–14th century cemeteries in the Volga-Ural region reports paternal and maternal lineages shared with Hungarian conquerors.

place.label: Volga region
place.note: Pin placed by Claude in the region the study names ('Russia (Volga)'). The cemetery's exact position has not been checked.

claims.text: The study reports that the paternal lineage N1a1-M46 “is present at all sites associated with the early Hungarians and among the conquerors”, but not in the Novinki group.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: It reports several maternal lineages that “represent a direct link between the groups from the Volga-Ural region and Carpathian Basin”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: It reports long-lasting genetic connections between sites of the Kushnarenkovo and the later Chiyalik cultures.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Most of the early Hungarian tribes originated from the Volga-Kama and South-Ural regions, and conquered the Carpathian Basin around 890.
claims.certainty_reason: The authors' framing, supported by their genetic links; one tier B study, no review checked.

claims.text: Hungarians who stayed behind in the Volga-Ural region were reported in the mid-13th century; archaeologists associate their remains with the Chiyalik culture, in the area known as Magna Hungaria.

held_by.who: Szeifert et al. (2022), summarising earlier archaeological research

claims.certainty_reason: A summary of earlier research in one tier B study; the 13th-century report itself has not been opened.

dating_methods.text: The study covers sites from the 6th to the 14th centuries; each site is dated by period in its Table 1.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
